analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence Afternoon Briefing (October 14, 2026)
key_insights: SPX fell 1.1%, NDX 2.0% and RTY 1.9% on Oct 14. SPX ended a 53-day streak without a 1%+ decline. RTY is 11% below its peak and in a correction. Cyclicals underperformed defensives by 7.0%.

The initial selloff was triggered by a hotter-than-expected September core CPI, but tech was the main driver of the day's decline. Semis, memory and hardware sold off. SOXX fell for a sixth straight day.

Treasuries sold off at the 8:30am ET CPI release, with the 2Y spiking nearly 16bp, then reversed almost entirely by the close (2Y +2bp, 10Y -2bp, 30Y -4bp). JPM saw no clear catalyst or dovish signal behind the reversal.

JPM gives three reasons for the yield reversal: wait for Thursday's PPI and Fedspeak before reading a Fed signal, the market overreacted when October hike odds jumped above 50% (now ~32%, with ~30bp of hikes priced through year-end), and there were signs of a move into quality and safe assets plus concern about a possible AI-related credit event.
October rate hike probability moved from ~20% to ~50% right after CPI, then fell back to about 33%.

AI was again the main challenge. ASML fell 3.9% despite a beat-and-raise, CoreWeave fell 15.5% as its 2032 unsecured bonds moved into distress, and a headline about an OpenAI staff departure intensified the selloff.

JPM sees potential for further de-grossing into key tech catalysts. TPM is at a neutral ~46th percentile versus ~19th percentile near the late-July low. JPM remains constructive on the sector and sees a possible opportunity to buy the dip.

Unrounded September core CPI was +0.335% m/m versus the Street's 0.2% and Feroli's 0.18%. JPM called it a hawkish print. The increase was broad across categories, with used cars, transportation and apparel standing out.
Chase card data and bank earnings show consumer demand remains elevated, which keeps core inflation sticky. JPM expects rate-sensitive baskets to stay under pressure in the short term.

JPM Economics (Reinhart) forecasts core PCE of 0.31% m/m (3.1% y/y, 2.8% 3m saar), which puts the October FOMC in play. They still expect the next hike in December. Core goods rose 0.25%, core services 0.37% and supercore 0.42%.

Headline CPI exceeded swap market pricing by over 7bp, the largest upside surprise since the March 2024 CPI report. Inflation data surprises over the past month now point to upside risk to inflation markets.

ETF desk (Rogerson): customers bought energy (MLPA, MLPX, AMLP, IEO) and growth (IWF block, VUG, VONG), and made opportunistic bids in DRAM. International products saw supply (EEM, IEMG, EFA, EWJ, FLJP). The desk expects the international supply trend to extend after CPI.
Tomorrow's PPI forecast from Feroli: headline +0.5% m/m (5.3% y/y), core +0.3% m/m (4.4% y/y), food PPI +0.7%. Retail sales forecast: headline +0.4%, control group +0.2%, driven by Chase card data.
BAC fell about 5% after a topline miss of about 3% driven by fee income. Equities revenue missed by 1.5% and FICC by 10%. Total trading was down 5% y/y versus GS +37%, C +6% and JPM +15%.
Financials desk: clients feel banks lose whether AI rises (flow of funds out of Fins) or fades (Fins exposed to AI financing). Positioning in banks had grown longer into earnings.

Tech desk: SMH down 80bp premarket while Mag 7 pushed higher, as models become interchangeable at the frontier and higher rates favor hyperscalers that can fund from FCF. ASML had margins well ahead of expectations, a higher Q4 guide, and customers ordering as far out as 2030.

DPZ: analyst Ivankoe stays Overweight with a Dec-27 PT of $350 after guidance reflected a reduction in unit growth. Restaurant positioning is extreme low: L/S ratio 0.5x, at the 1st percentile since 2018.

JPM Market Intel stays Tactically Bullish into earnings. SOX is about 20% off its July lows and 15% below its June ATHs. JPM expects semis to recover on Hynix and Samsung strength and thinks deteriorating breadth can reverse.

Monetization Menu (Oct 12) prefers Tech and some Cyclicals with a bullish global AI view. Reopening themes to focus on are Cruise Lines, Hotels and Retailers. Internationally, JPM likes Brazil and Japan.

Earlier menus: JPM no longer pairs long Tech with a short RTY because of squeeze risk from lower oil or yields, and prefers derivative expressions. A US/Iran deal is the biggest catalyst and would squeeze EU and RTY higher.

Oct 15 catalysts: TSMC guidance, PPI, retail sales and jobless claims at 8:30am ET, and Warsh's final remarks in Bangkok after the close before the FOMC. Earnings: AA, BNY, IBKR, JBHT, MRSH, PLD, PNC, SCHW, USB.

Cross-asset moves: WTI +1.0% to $95.09, silver -6.1% (worst day since June) to $55.56, gold -1.7% to $4,105, NatGas -2.6% to $3.20, 10Y at 5.185%, VIX 16.87. Europe held up better: EZU -0.8%, UKX +0.7%, SX5E +0.4%.

market_movers.rationale: Trading desk calls the print 'really disappointing': topline miss of about 3% on fee income, equities missed by 1.5%, FICC by 10%, total trading down 5% y/y. Expects market pressure on management.
Ivankoe stays OW with a Dec-27 PT of $350 after guidance reflected a slowdown in unit growth. Focus is on FCF.
Strong quarter with margins well ahead of expectations, a higher Q4 guide and orders placed as far out as 2030. The stock still fell 3.9%.
Stock fell 15.5% as its 2032 unsecured bonds moved into distress.

sector_views.rationale: Tactically Bullish into earnings. Semis can climb the wall of worry on Hynix and Samsung strength, with a possible buy-the-dip opportunity despite de-grossing risk.
Cyclicals need a bull-steepening yield curve and strong bank earnings to rally persistently. Reopening names (Cruise Lines, Hotels, Retailers) are favored for consumer strength.
Desk sees sloppy action, with banks caught between AI flow-of-funds selling and AI-financing exposure. The older menu favored Banks ex-AI on growth, steeper curve and capital markets.
Likely to lag the SPX ex-AI plays, though they may join a squeeze.
Positioning is extremely low, with an L/S ratio of 0.5x at the 1st percentile since 2018.

earnings_insights: BAC reported Q3 on 10/14: topline about 3% below consensus on fee income. Equities revenue missed by 1.5% and FICC by 10%. Total trading was -5% y/y versus GS +37%, C +6% and JPM +15%. Expenses also missed, with some AML-related noise.
ASML reported 10/14: margins well ahead of expectations and an increase to the Q4 guide. Management cited order visibility out to 2030 and plans to add supply capacity.
DPZ reported 10/13: guidance reflects a reduction in unit growth. Comps are a leading indicator of development. Unit development slowdown and supply benefits are now behind the company.
Upcoming earnings: Oct 15 AA, BNY, IBKR, JBHT, MRSH, PLD, PNC, SCHW, USB. Oct 16 CFG, TFC, TRV. TSMC guidance is due Oct 15.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above the Street's 0.2% and Feroli's 0.18%, read as hawkish, broad-based across categories.
Firm enough to put the October FOMC in play, though JPM expects the next hike in December.
Three-month pace of 2.2% is back near last year's highs.
Supercore increased, adding to the broad inflation pressure.
Food PPI is seen accelerating to 0.7%, with an Ag inflation spike expected into year-end and 27Q1.
PPI will help verify the full picture on PCE.
Driven by strength in Chase card data.
Consumer concerns make this a number to watch.
Market overreacted initially. About 30bp of hikes are priced through year-end.
Yields reversed from the morning spike.
